cases.question: Compare retry_if_result.__call__ and retry_if_not_result.__call__: what happens when outcome is missing, when the outcome failed, and when it succeeded?
cases.expected_answer: Both raise RuntimeError for missing outcome; both return False for failed outcomes without calling the result predicate. On success retry_if_result returns predicate(outcome.result()), while retry_if_not_result returns its boolean negation.
required_details: Failed outcomes return False in both strategies
Failed outcomes do not invoke predicate

cases.question: In retry_if_exception_cause_type.__call__, does matching the raised exception itself trigger retry, how are deeper causes and cycles handled, and what happens for a missing or successful outcome?
cases.expected_answer: Missing outcome raises RuntimeError. A successful outcome returns False. For failure it starts at outcome.exception(), but tests exc.__cause__ rather than exc itself; a matching raised exception alone with no matching cause returns False. It follows explicit __cause__ links, returns True on any matching cause, and records id(exc) in seen to stop on cycles or None, returning False if no cause matched.
required_details: Raised exception itself is not the tested object

cases.question: In get_path, how does a dotted string path access a numeric list index, which lookup errors are wrapped, and how do an omitted default and an explicit None default differ?
cases.expected_answer: String paths split on dots and traversal indexes cur[seg]. KeyError/IndexError immediately become PathAccessError. Only TypeError tries int(seg) then re-indexes, enabling numeric string list indexes; a mapping KeyError for a numeric string is not retried as an integer. Failed conversion/re-indexing becomes PathAccessError, with a non-indexable object message when cur is not iterable. An outer PathAccessError is re-raised when default is the _UNSET sentinel; any explicit default, including None, is returned. Successful traversal returns cur.
required_details: KeyError and IndexError wrapped without integer fallback

cases.question: In LRU.__getitem__, what changes on a hit, on a miss without on_miss, when on_miss returns, and when on_miss raises?
cases.expected_answer: Under the lock it gets the link and moves it to the most recently used position. Hit increments hit_count and returns link[VALUE]. A KeyError increments miss_count before checking on_miss; without a truthy callback it re-raises. With callback it evaluates on_miss(key), stores the returned value via self[key] assignment and returns it without incrementing hit_count for this miss. If callback raises, it propagates and no returned value is inserted; miss_count remains incremented.
required_details: Hit moves entry to recent position
Hit increments hit_count and returns stored value
Callback result inserted and returned without hit increment
Callback exception propagates without inserting value
